parsed.explanation: The parent regime imposes real traveller-facing exposures: passport rules eliminate X markers and process only birth-sex markers, entry officers may refuse applicants whose documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and consider lifetime fraud findings, foreign governments issue trans-specific travel advisories, and facility bans (with criminal exposure in 4 states and a documented arrest) apply in many states, while custody practices document severe abuse. That parent regime alone sits around 0.35–0.40. The division, however, adds documented territory-specific mitigations: a care-access sanctuary shield that expressly protects travelling families, identity-based prison housing with funded surgery (documented to 2021, currency unresolved), and a top-tier protective-law rating. Against that, it records the highest raw anti-LGBTQ incident count of any sub-unit and a rising hate-crime trend in its largest city — but with no per-capita denominator, this carries limited magnitude. The division-specific positives move it materially above the parent average, while the unquantified hostility record and unresolved prison-policy currency pull it back down: 0.55.
